response.sql:
WITH filtered_tracks AS (
  SELECT 
    mt.MediaTypeId,
    mt.Name,
    t.UnitPrice,
    CASE WHEN t.Bytes IS NOT NULL 
         THEN CAST(t.Bytes AS DECIMAL) / t.Milliseconds 
         ELSE NULL 
    END as bytes_per_ms
  FROM Track t
  INNER JOIN MediaType mt ON t.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId
  WHERE t.Bytes >= 10323804
),
media_type_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    MediaTypeId,
    Name,
    AVG(UnitPrice) as avg_unit_price,
    AVG(bytes_per_ms) as avg_bytes_per_ms
  FROM filtered_tracks
  GROUP BY MediaTypeId, Name
),
global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_bytes_per_ms) as global_avg_bytes_per_ms
  FROM media_type_stats
)
SELECT 
  mts.Name,
  mts.avg_unit_price,
  mts.avg_bytes_per_ms,
  mts.avg_bytes_per_ms / ga.global_avg_bytes_per_ms as ratio
FROM media_type_stats mts
CROSS JOIN global_avg ga
WHERE ga.global_avg_bytes_per_ms IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: Track.Milliseconds is never zero, ensuring the division (Track.Bytes ÷ Track.Milliseconds) is always valid. The schema does not constrain this, but it is a reasonable assumption for track duration data.

alternatives.interpretation: The phrase 'the plain average of it across all the media types' could mean the overall average of bytes_per_ms calculated from all filtered tracks (weighted by track count), rather than the unweighted average of the per-media-type averages.
